main_body: Beehive-shaped thatched hut: a large conical thatch roof (rows 2-57) over a short clay wall (rows 57-77) with an arched doorway
top_band: Thatch roof in golden-yellow tones, rows ~2-56. Its slope is shown as stacked courses lighter at the top-left and darker to the right, and it overhangs the wall at the eave
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the thatch slope is a large, clearly visible roof surface. It ends in a dark brown eave line at rows ~55-57, with a shadowed strip under the overhang at rows ~57-60. Below that is the clay wall, which has its own shading and brick-like texture. The door is inset: it has a brown frame, a lintel and a dark interior, and the arched opening is cut into the thatch. Both the roof surface and the front face are clearly drawn, as in the house references.

style.evidence: The thatch has about five tones, with per-course highlights, dark gaps between courses and tuft dots. The wall carries brick streaks and a mottled gradient, and the base is a speckled stone strip. The outline is dark brown, matching the adjacent thatch and clay rather than a neutral black. The only flat area is the dark door interior, which is acceptable. Tile density is comparable to the references.
